issues.situation: Home objective. reinforce_cap_price also discounts insurance on our own home objective. That includes primary_awareness's hold_home_required +3 and secondary_defend_home. When a primary rule has require_hold_home, losing home costs the whole per-objective bonus (the AI's own note: 'my home objective must stay held for the per-objective bonus'), not just the scaled terms. LONE-TRIP and FAR-TRIP both exempt home ('home is never skipped').
issues.proposed_change: In reinforce_cap_price, after the state check, add: if ev.get("is_home", false): return {}. This does not change the s7437 decision (centre) or any guardrail.

issues.situation: Loaded enemy transport. projected_enemy_oc and projected_max_oc skip embarked units, which have no on-board centroid, so a transport counts only its own OC. Example: a Battlewagon (OC 5) carrying 5 Kommandos (OC 5) is one move from a centre held with OC 6. It passes 'no single unit can contest alone' (5 < 6) with share 25%, so Beta is redirected. Transport plus disembark then brings 10 OC in one move. Base would have added about 9 OC of insurance (15 > 10). None of the 325 saved rollout positions contains a loaded transport, so the bundle test cannot catch this; human players can trigger it.
issues.proposed_change: In reinforce_cap_price, return {} when any enemy unit inside the COORD-5 projection radius has a non-empty transport_data.embarked_units (the AI already reads this at the is_loaded_transport check, ~line 7240). Alternatively, record cargo OC in a fix-only eval field and add it to largest and proj.

issues.situation: rc_reopened is too broad. Pass 2.5 sets rc_reopened[a_oid] for any attack conversion. That includes a this-turn mover such as Gamma (Custodian Guard are melee seekers) whose OC was never in friendly_oc. The backfill then skips the cap, and OBJ-BACKFILL-1 switches Beta back to the centre at full score (48.2 > 30.7). This undoes the redirect although the holders and the threat are unchanged. The result is base behaviour, not worse than base, but it shrinks the fix exactly in its target matchup.
issues.proposed_change: Set rc_reopened[a_oid] = true only when the converted assignment's action was "hold". That is the only case where its OC was in friendly_oc and held is overstated. A converted mover is already dropped from held because its action becomes "attack".

issues.situation: Greedy pre-emption. The redirect applies the alternative at once (apply_capture_assignment) at Beta's alt score (30.7). It does this before other unassigned units whose higher-scoring candidates for that objective (e.g. 35 < 48.2) come later in the sorted list. If Beta covers the need, the better-suited unit finds remaining 0 and drops to its next option, possibly the same insurance or a slower trip. The result is a role swap with a later arrival. It did not happen at s7437 (Alpha still went to obj_nml_2). The existing OVERCOMMIT redirect has the same pattern.
issues.proposed_change: In reinforce_cap_redirect, skip an alternative objective when still-unassigned units with a higher candidate score there (score > alt.score) already cover its obj_oc_remaining (sum of their unit_oc >= remaining). Alternatively, re-queue the capped candidate at its price instead of redirecting immediately.

issues.situation: OBJ-ASSIGN-1 bypasses the cap. Suppose unit U's capped reinforcement finds no redirect. OBJ-ASSIGN-1 can then hand the insurance to a quicker unit V at full price without pricing V's candidate. V may have a better objective that still needs OC. U, which had nothing better, then falls through to its next option. This is the opposite of 'the need stays open for a unit with less to gain elsewhere'.
issues.proposed_change: In the OBJ-ASSIGN-1 alt loop, add: var v_price: Dictionary = reinforce_cap_price.call(alt); if not v_price.is_empty() and not (reinforce_cap_redirect.call(alt, float(v_price.score)) as Dictionary).is_empty(): continue.

issues.situation: Silent decision change. The COORD-4 backfill guard ('continue  # REINFORCE-CAP: a switch to insurance is judged at the insurance price') changes a decision with no log line. The project rule asks for a tagged log line whenever new logic changes a decision. Test T1 relies on this guard implicitly: without it, beta would switch back to obj_x.
issues.proposed_change: Before the continue, print one line: "AIDecisionMaker: [REINFORCE-CAP] %s: %s stays on %s — switching to it is worth %.1f as insurance, not %.1f (current %.1f)" % [cand.objective_id, cand.unit_id, cur.objective_id, bf_price.score, cand.score, cur.score].

issues.situation: Test coverage gaps. The test pins and erases the override, drives _evaluate_all_objectives and _assign_units_to_objectives (the real planner), and its 8 base failures are the right ones. But it does not cover: (a) a holder converting to attack, after which the re-opened objective is reinforced at full price; (b) an open alternative that scores below the insurance price, where the unit should still reinforce; (c) the actual s7437 mechanism, a 3-turn walk paced to a 2-turn Advance that RACE-SKIP no longer vetoes. T6 is a 2-turn trip at both paces, so it tests only the move/advance choice.
issues.proposed_change: Add three cases: (a) a movable holder with a melee target in reach plus a capped reinforcer, asserting the reinforcer is allowed back; (b) obj_side made low-value (e.g. far, or no NML bonus) so price > alt, asserting beta reinforces obj_x; (c) beta about 20" from obj_side at M6 with a lost race, asserting an advance capture where base gives RACE-SKIP.

summary:
Verdict: ok. I found no real bug and the test does test the fix. I was told not to run Godot, so the unit-test pass counts are the fix agent's. Everything else below I checked myself.

Code:
- Setting FIX_REINFORCE_CAP=0 gives base behaviour exactly. reinforce_cap_price returns {} when rc_on is false. The redirect, _reinforce_cap_paced and the backfill guard are reachable only through it. Neither projected_max_oc nor rc_reopened is read anywhere else.
- Patch file and commit c6d4d5d are identical. The diff only adds lines, so no debug log was removed.
- Null access: str() wraps special_rules, which is null on the Tankbusta Standard weapon. Missing fields use defaults (projected_max_oc falls back to proj).
- Ids and double counting: held = friendly_oc plus this-turn arrivals, excluding the unit itself. COORD-2 en-route units are correctly left out, since they cannot be in range during the enemy turn. Every movable unit on a held_threatened objective is held in pass 1, so friendly_oc stays accurate. Held_safe objectives never reach the cap because their need is 0.
- Earmarks: the label is set only for a plan pointing at that same objective.
- Cost: a few dictionary scans per candidate, so negligible.
- Style: lambdas, tags and the 'x in special_rules' check all match the surrounding code (e.g. OVERCOMMIT).
- Check of the s7437 log numbers: price 17.2 = 48.2 - 0.75 x 41.4 (hold terms); share = (0+7-6+1)/8 = 0.25.

Test:
- Pins FIX_REINFORCE_CAP=1, erases it at the end, and drives the real planner functions.
- Tracing its 13 asserts on base gives exactly 5 pass and 8 fail, and every failure is 'beta reinforces instead of redirecting'.
- T1 also exercises the backfill guard implicitly.

Data:
- The checks agree with the rollout files on disk. f1_ab: A 14/3 vs B 7/22. Final fix: 7 and 22 on seeds 5001/5002, identical to B.
- Fix minus base on 5001-5004: -7, +19, -5, -10 (mean -0.75, n=4, noisy). The case for the fix rests on the 36-seed +4.36 [0.61, 8.12] for the same forced decision.
- [REINFORCE-CAP] fired once per seed at s7437 and 0 times in f2, g1-g4 and xg1, whose values match base.

Minor issues, all with concrete changes:
1. Exempt home objectives (require_hold_home can make losing home cost far more than the discounted terms).
2. Skip the cap when a projected enemy transport is loaded (cargo is invisible to the projection; no saved position has one, so the bundle test cannot catch it).
3. Set rc_reopened only when a holder converts, not a this-turn mover.
4. The redirect can pre-empt a better-suited unit on the alternative objective.
5. OBJ-ASSIGN-1 can hand the insurance to a quicker unit without pricing it.
6. Add a log line to the backfill guard.
7. Three test gaps.

Unmodelled risk (already the fix agent's risk 1): the share model ignores attrition of the holders. At s7437 one Allarus casualty leaves OC 4, and the Battlewagon (OC 5) could then contest alone.

Recommendation: fine for the round-3 bundle test as is. Add guards 1-3 before a player release.

Screenshot: n/a. This was a read-only code review; Godot was not run, per the task.

issues.situation: The cap's premise is that no single enemy unit can contest the objective alone and the enemy probably cannot bring enough OC. It is false at the finding itself (s7437 R2 P1, Custodes vs Orks). COORD-5's projection only counts units whose centroid is within M+2"+3.79": Battlewagon Beta, Mek Beta and Zodgrod, 7 OC, largest unit 5, so the cap reads a ~25% chance. Measured from the save, two units outside that list could each take the centre alone with an average Advance (M6+3.5"): Gretchin (10 OC, nearest model 11.4") and Lootas Alpha (10 OC, nearest model 9.9"). The Ork OC really within reach is about 32, not 7. In the fix's own replays the Ork AI advanced Gretchin onto the centre in seeds 5001, 5002 and 5003 ('flipping it'), and in seed 5003 Gretchin secured the centre (Thievin' Scavengers). In the base replay of seed 5003 the Orks sent Gretchin and then Lootas Gamma against a 12-OC hold ('needs 3 more OC after this unit'). The enemy AI fills its flip need on purpose; it does not arrive uniformly over 0..P as the share model assumes. The cap fires at its evidence only because of this blind spot.
issues.proposed_change: Do not merge REINFORCE-CAP into V9 (keep FIX_REINFORCE_CAP=0). Any honest correction removes the fire at the finding: compute largest/proj for the cap over enemy units whose nearest model reaches control range with M + ADVANCE_EXPECTED_EXTRA_INCHES. That would leave this cluster with no general fix in this form, so treat it as dropped.

issues.situation: The cap assumes the holders stay. It only bites on held_threatened objectives (an enemy centroid within 12"; held_safe objectives have zero need in pass 2), so the holders nearly always have charge targets. The charge phase is planned separately, and CH-LEAVE only multiplies the charge score by 0.5. In all 4 fixed replays the Allarus, now the centre's sole holders, declared charges off it: 8-17% odds, final scores 0.3-0.6, 1 CP spent on Fury of the Emperor. In seeds 5003 and 5004 the charge succeeded. In seed 5004 the Orks held the centre at their R2 movement and scored +4 per_objective at their R2 command, which base did not give up. In seed 5003 P1 had 2 OC left on the centre, Gretchin secured it, and P1 lost Centre Ground (5 VP) at R2. In base the Allarus also charged (3 of 4 seeds) but Beta kept the centre. Within this game family the insurance turned out to be needed in half the replays, for a reason the share model does not contain.
issues.proposed_change: If a reinforcement cap is ever kept, count in `held` only holders with no charge target outside the objective's range (this also stops the fire at the finding). Do NOT instead veto the holders' charges after a cap: at s7418 R3 P2 (asymmetric fixture, a position where the cap's gate is met: Ork centre 10 OC against ~17 projected, largest 9, share 0.44), 'Hold obj_center' instead of attacking out was measured harmful at -8.33 [-12.33, -4.34] over 12 seeds.

issues.situation: The measured gain (+4.36 over 36 seeds) comes from a card-specific mechanism, but the cap ignores cards. P1's primary at s7437 is Reconnaissance Sweep. It pays 3/6 VP at end of turn for units in 3/4 table quarters (wholly within the quarter and more than 6" from the centre). The centre was only 'insurance for hold-1', because obj_nml_1 already met hold_min. The fix agent's A/B attributes B's gain to quarters, kills and A Tempting Target. Against base, the fix gained +3 quarters at R2 end of turn in all 4 seeds, and the walking variant, which stopped on the quarter line, measured -4.0. The bench rotates 25 disposition pairings, and Reconnaissance Sweep is the decider's card in only 1 of them. In 7 pairings the primary pays 3-6 VP per held objective per command phase; in 5 more it has a hold_more rule. There, a held objective lost in the enemy turn costs every remaining round. A one-round rollout from R2 cannot see R4-R5, which is the round-2 lesson.
issues.proposed_change: Re-target the cluster at the mechanism the evidence supports, and measure each fix on its own: (a) a rules fix so that _should_unit_advance and _should_unit_advance_long_trip treat [ASSAULT] ranged weapons as no shooting cost, with its own failing-first test; (b) value an uncovered table quarter for quarter-scoring cards (Reconnaissance Sweep primary, Engage on All Fronts secondary) with the card's own test, near its VP, instead of the flat 4.2 `secondary_spread` bonus on the estimated destination point.

issues.situation: The cap fires rarely and its fires overlap the other round-3 fix, so the bundle test cannot measure it. My scan used approximate OC (no 11e terrain-area rule) and ignored the score condition. It found about 3 distinct gate hits with a 1-turn reinforcer in bench matchups across ~440 saved movement positions (204 rollout cases and 240 sweep positions): s7437 R2 P1, s7418 R3 P2, s7401 R3 P1. It also fires in the keeper_release trajectory: in several keeper replays the R2 P1 Beta reinforcement of the Allarus-held centre has share 0.25-0.50. Its effect is therefore confounded with FIX_KEEPER in the same Custodes vs Orks openings.
issues.proposed_change: If the parent still bundles it, give it its own switch-off arm and count [REINFORCE-CAP] lines per game, so a null or negative result can be traced to it.

issues.situation: After a redirect, the need on the held objective stays open at full price for units that arrive in 2 or more turns, because reinforce_cap_price skips turns_to_reach > 1. At the finding, Gamma (21.8" away, a 3-turn trip) took the centre's 2-OC need in pass 2. A late arrival cannot insure the next enemy turn, and this pattern can produce crossing assignments: the close unit goes far, the far unit goes to the 'safe' objective. The redirected assignment also skips OBJ-ASSIGN-1's quicker-unit check. It made no difference at the finding (base sent Gamma via the support pass).
issues.proposed_change: If a cap survives, apply it with turns_to_reach > 1 as well (or reduce the open need by the capped unit's OC x (1 - share)), and run OBJ-ASSIGN-1 on the redirect target.

summary:
Verdict: drop. REINFORCE-CAP does reproduce the measured alternative at s7437 (+4.36 over 36 seeds), but the reason it gives is false at that same position, and the gain comes from something else.

1. **The threat set is incomplete.** COORD-5 lists 7 enemy OC with the largest unit at 5. From the save, Gretchin (10 OC) and Lootas Alpha (10 OC) can each take the 6-OC centre alone with an average Advance. The Ork AI advanced Gretchin onto the centre in 3 of the 4 fixed replays and secured it in seed 5003.
2. **The holders do not stay.** The Allarus declared charges off the centre in 4 of 4 fixed replays (CH-LEAVE only halves the score) and left it in 2. Seed 5004: P2 scored +4 per_objective at its R2 command, which base did not give up. Seed 5003: P1 lost Centre Ground at R2.
3. **The gain is tied to one card.** It came from table quarters under Reconnaissance Sweep (the walking variant that missed the quarter measured -4.0). That card is the decider's primary in only 1 of the 25 bench pairings. In 12 pairings each held objective pays every round.

Any coherent revision (an Advance-reach threat set, or not counting holders that will charge off) stops the cap from firing at the finding. Vetoing the holders' charges instead conflicts with a measured guardrail: at s7418 R3 P2, a position where the cap's gate is met, holding instead of attacking out scored -8.33. The cap also fires rarely (about 3 gate hits in ~440 saved full-game movement positions), and in the s7437 openings it overlaps keeper_release, so the round-3 bundle cannot measure it.

Recommendation: keep FIX_REINFORCE_CAP=0, leave it out of V9, and re-target the cluster as two separately measured fixes: an [ASSAULT]-aware Advance rules fix, and card-based valuation of table quarters.

What I did: read-only analysis of the code, the fix's own replay logs and records, and the saved positions. I did not run Godot. No measured position conflicts with the cap's own decisions. The frequency scan uses approximate OC (it ignores the 11e terrain-area rule).
